replies.author: @XJN758
replies.text: ​@Kit456mine, Russian history and statehood began in 862, nearly four centuries before the Mongol invasion, starting with the foundation of Rus' in Novgorod and Kyiv. Moscow and most other Russian cities were founded during this pre-Mongol era, and the Russian population genetically and culturally stems from eastern Slavic tribes like the Krivichs and Vyatichs. If you are trying to frame Moscow as a 'Mongol project,' remember that Kyiv, Chernigov, and Vladimir had the exact same status under the Golden Horde. They were not integrated into the Empire as domestic provinces; rather, the Mongols maintained them as autonomous vassal principalities to exact tribute. The Mongols often operated this way with conquered states — for instance, before they directly established the Yuan dynasty in China, they heavily relied on local administrations and puppet rulers.
